text:
amanda: heads up — I noticed the fast-nav org switch (top-left selector) can surface other org's saved searches briefly after switching. repro steps: click fast nav -> choose org B -> dropdown shows results for org A for ~1s then updates. Noticed in prod on Canary 3. :grimacing:
ryan: ugh. seen that in local a while ago when we made client-side caching for search entries. Could be stale cache keying. Which page did you repro from?
amanda: Reports > Saved Searches. Happens when you open the nav while the search cache is still warming. I can repro consistently with heavy client side caching enabled.
sylvia: is the cache scoped by workspace_id? we had a bug earlier where we used user_id only and that caused cross-workspace flashes.
amanda: looks like cache key is `recentNav` + user_id. not including workspace. quick dump from console: ```localStorage.getItem('recentNav') => [{id:'s-123',label:'eng runs',org: 'org-A'}]```
mike: that explains it. client-side cache needs workspace prefix OR we should invalidate on org-switch. Which is better?
neil: prefixing is safer long-term. invalidation has edge cases (lost updates). if we add workspace to keys, we avoid rehydration flashes. but also worried about telemetry: need to ensure we don't leak org ids into any shared telemetry events.
amanda: good point. I saw some telemetry events emitted from nav load that have `last_search_id` field. It contained IDs from the previous org during the flash. Not currently PII but that's definitely cross-tenant fuzz.yan: internal-api debate: do we rely on client to include X-Workspace header on quick-nav requests, or enforce server-side session tenant for those endpoints? Right now quick-nav hits `GET /api/ui/nav` which trusts session. Client cache is just UI-level.
sylvia: server-side enforcement is stricter but will not stop UI flashes caused by localStorage rehydrate before server response. So both: scope cache keys and make server return 400 if client passes mismatched workspace in body.
mike: rollout plan idea: patch UI to namespace localStorage keys by workspace_id and add a short debounce on rehydrate to wait for `GET /api/session` result (100ms). Then release server check as follow-up. Can canary 10% orgs first.
amanda: I can PR the UI change today. small patch: change key to `recentNav:v2:{workspace_id}` and add fallback migration code to drop old entries with mismatched workspace.
eil: telemetry changes: redact last_search_id from UI telemetry until we confirm no cross-org values. Also add a metric `ui.nav.stale_flash` that increments if UI detects cached entries with different workspace than session.yan: good. ops note: deploy-bot will run canary after mergebot. @deploy-bot can you schedule a 10% rollout for eng-console on patch?
deploy-bot: scheduling canary rollout: eng-console v3.14.2 -> canary 10% at 2024-03-02T15:20:00Z. Monitoring windows: 20m.
sylvia: after canary, let's check console-telemetry for spikes in `ui.nav.error` and `ui.nav.stale_flash`. If clean, increase to 50% then 100% in separate rollouts.
mike: quick UX note — the debounce shouldn't add perceptible latency. 100ms will avoid the flash but keep navigation feeling snappy.
amanda: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/console/pull/4872 (UI cache scoping + migration + telemetry flag). Requesting review from @ryan and @sylvia.yan: reviewing now. If green, merge and I'll queue deploy. Thanks for catching this, Amanda. :thumbsup:
amanda: thanks all. I'll follow up with a short postmortem snippet in #incidents if we see any confirmed cross-tenant telemetry hits.
